sentences.text: The name Secernosaurus translates to 'separated reptile,' a title reflecting its geographic isolation from relatives in the Northern Hemisphere.
The specific name koerneri honors the paleontologist Harold E. Koerner.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measures approximately 4 to 5 meters in length and likely represents a mature individual.

This dinosaur is distinguished by a subhorizontal crest on the ilium separating the preacetabular notch from the pubic pedicle, a longitudinal crest on the dorsal surface of the postacetabular process, and a twisted distal end of that process.
The holotype specimen was collected in 1923 during an expedition led by J. B. Abbott.
The genus was formally named by Brett-Surman in 1979.
Secernosaurus koerneri was the first formally named hadrosaurid species from South America.
Only one fossil occurrence of Secernosaurus has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Secernosaurus was a herbivorous hadrosaurid dinosaur.
The neuroanatomy of Secernosaurus koerneri is very similar to that of Northern Hemisphere hadrosaurids.
Secernosaurus is a member of the family Hadrosauridae.
It is classified within the duck-billed dinosaur family Hadrosauridae.
Secernosaurus is a member of the bird-hipped dinosaur class Ornithischia.
Phylogenetic analyses classify Secernosaurus within the hadrosaurid tribe Kritosaurini and subfamily Saurolophinae.
Secernosaurus belongs to the tribe Kritosaurini.
Secernosaurus is classified within the subfamily Saurolophinae.
Secernosaurus belongs to the subfamily Kritosaurini.
The type species of the genus Secernosaurus is Secernosaurus koerneri.
Secernosaurus lived in South America, a region distinct from the Laurasian continents where most other hadrosaurids lived.
Secernosaurus koerneri lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now South America.
Secernosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
Secernosaurus fossils are found in the uppermost part of the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation.
Palynological data suggest the climate in the upper deposits of the formation was mild with balanced wet and dry seasons during the end of the Cretaceous and Paleocene.
Researchers suggest Secernosaurus arrived in South America via a dispersal event from North America during the Campanian, possibly using the proto-Antilles island chain.
Fossils of Secernosaurus have been found in the Lago Colhué Huapi and Los Alamitos formations.
Recent evidence in 2022 suggests that Secernosaurus koerneri, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, and 'Kritosaurus' australis are valid taxa.
Researchers note that the history of hadrosaurs on Gondwanan landmasses is still poorly understood.
